title: Plastic consumption and waste require a common life-cycle accounting system before circular-economy policy can be compared
source_unit: UNEP and UNITAR, Statistical Guideline for Measuring Flows of Plastic throughout the Life Cycle
geography: National, regional, and global plastic production, trade, consumption, and waste statistics

denominator.unit: global, regional, and national plastic-flow statistical system

measurement_gap.value: A detailed, globally agreed methodology for measuring plastic flows has been lacking

life_cycle_scope.value: The guideline covers production, trade, consumption, and waste across the plastic life cycle

policy_relevance.value: Comparable plastic statistics are intended to support circular-economy, source-inventory, waste-management, and SDG policymaking

observations.method: UNEP-UNITAR statistical guidance developed with international organizations, national statistical offices, ministries, academia, research institutes, and other Member State experts, aligned to international standards and available data sources.
observations.uncertainty: The guideline is a first step and states that some aspects require further discussion and refinement; availability, quality, and comparability of national data remain open.
observations.subgroup: Statistical offices, environmental agencies, producers, traders, consumers, waste managers, workers, communities, and policymakers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Existing national data may support useful action before full global comparability, and a common methodology can still miss informal, illegal, or poorly documented flows.

boundary_definition.value: The guideline defines boundaries, key terms, concepts, and main accounting elements for plastic flows

flow_stages.value: Production, international and domestic trade, consumption, use, collection, treatment, and waste are connected as a life-cycle system

linear_economy.value: Plastic production and consumption continue to operate in a predominantly linear economy with insufficient waste management

observations.method: Life-cycle statistical framework intended to make material boundaries and flow stages explicit and comparable across national, regional, and global accounts.
observations.uncertainty: Accounting for a flow does not establish environmental harm, exposure, recycling quality, worker conditions, or consumer welfare at each stage; definitions and loss estimates can still vary.
observations.subgroup: Plastic-producing sectors, importers and exporters, retailers, households, waste workers, municipalities, recyclers, and communities near production or disposal sites.
observations.counterinterpretation: A linear flow can include products with long service lives or technically recoverable materials; the statistical pattern is not itself a complete measure of circularity or harm.

consumer_visibility.value: Life-cycle statistics can make the material consequences of consumption more visible beyond point-of-sale demand

producer_visibility.value: Comparable flow accounting can clarify sector and supply-chain responsibility for production, trade, and waste

policy_choice.value: Better flow data can support decisions on source reduction, product design, reuse, recycling, waste infrastructure, and regulation

observations.method: UNEP-UNITAR translation of statistical definitions into national and regional policy use for circular economy and plastic-waste management.
observations.uncertainty: Information visibility does not guarantee behavior change, producer responsibility, affordable alternatives, enforcement, or reduced plastic pollution.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, firms, regulators, public-procurement bodies, waste authorities, informal waste workers, and communities affected by plastic leakage.
observations.counterinterpretation: Data-driven regulation can shift costs to consumers or small firms and can privilege formal actors if informal recycling and repair work are not counted.

denominator.unit: plastic statistics production and governance capacity frame

institutional_users.value: Statistical offices and other organizations responsible for producing official plastics statistics are primary intended users

comparability.value: The guideline aims to produce high-quality statistics comparable across countries, regions, and the global level

future_revision.value: Application is expected to generate learning and future refinement of the methodology

observations.method: International statistical standard-setting and methodological guidance, with national application expected to test definitions, data sources, and accounting practice.
observations.uncertainty: The publication does not provide a global implementation rate, country-by-country data quality score, causal effect of adoption, or proof that comparable statistics are already available.
observations.subgroup: National statistical systems, environmental ministries, customs and trade agencies, local governments, researchers, civil society, and affected communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Standardization can improve accountability but can also create reporting burdens, reduce attention to local knowledge, or delay action while methods are being harmonized.

related_sources.claim: Complementary UNEP finance-flow evidence on nature-negative capital and environmental transition.
Complementary UNEP guidance on disaggregated environmental indicators and localized action.

boundary: This record adds a plastic life-cycle accounting, consumer-production, waste-infrastructure, and circular-economy governance route. It uses a statistical guideline, not a completed global dataset, individual purchase histories, household exposure records, project-level pollution outcomes, causal behavior effects, or proof that standardization produces lower plastic waste.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNEP publication page reviewed for the 2026 date, measurement gap, life-cycle boundaries, production-trade-consumption-waste accounting, international statistical alignment, national comparability, policy uses, and first-step/refinement caveat.
